A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAVAS work, with matching core equations and experiments. The supplied text and graphics are readable throughout. v1 ends after its references; v2 additionally contains Supplementary Material A–J.

before.justification: v1 reports original audio-generation comparisons, a 15-participant user study, component ablations, and qualitative examples in Tables 1–3 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation experiments, reports a 27-participant user study, and supplies additional estimator, robustness, runtime, and subgroup results in its supplement.

M1.justification: The PPE, mass/velocity conditioning, FiLM modulation, gated pooling, residual Delta-modulation, and flow-matching objective remain unchanged. Appendix E supplies implementation and architectural details without establishing a changed generation procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix B newly documents evaluation on ABO-500 objects for mass estimation and STARSS23 scenes for metric-displacement estimation as a velocity proxy. This substantially expands the documented dataset coverage beyond VGGSound and VGG-Impact. VGG-NonImpact merely subdivides previously covered VGGSound data.

E2.justification: The main V2A comparator sets remain unchanged. Appendix B supplies an expanded estimator comparison: Table S1 includes Image2mass, 2D CNN, and LLaVA alongside NeRF2Physics. Figure S1 explicitly compares against SpatialVLM's pseudo-ground-truth construction pipeline, clarifying the expert-model comparison invoked in v1.

E3.justification: Table 2 explicitly increases participation from 15 to 27 people. Newly included evaluations specify 500 ABO objects, 256 filtered STARSS23 clips with shared masks and displacement-tolerance metrics, inference-time physics perturbations, and runtime profiling over 100 videos. The core training settings stated in both main texts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds mass/velocity perturbation tests, complete physics-cue removal, APCC shuffling and noise checks, model-capacity comparisons, impact/non-impact breakdowns, and additional qualitative cases. These investigate robustness, metric validity, scaling, and applicability beyond the unchanged component ablations in Table 3.

E5.justification: Both versions report user-study means and standard deviations. v2 changes the participant count and resulting estimates but adds no repeated-run or seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain their numerical results, while Table 2 is revised for the expanded study; PAVAS physical plausibility changes from 4.34±0.86 to 4.37±0.84. Substantial new results include estimator accuracy, fallback performance, scaling, subgroup comparisons, runtime, and APCC degradation from 0.378 to 0.655 under shuffling. These are additional findings, not improvements to the unchanged main benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 makes the previously verbal APCC definition mathematically explicit, specifying incoming/outgoing event velocities and the class-averaged absolute correlation discrepancy. This adds formal specification beyond a standard correlation formula. The original method equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: physics-conditioned PAVAS, VGG-Impact, APCC, and improved physical consistency and perceptual quality. The supplement principally supports and qualifies these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and applicability discussion: velocity validation uses a displacement proxy; imperfect or missing physics cues permit fallback; text conditioning supports off-screen sounds; and CUT3R dominates computational overhead, with real-time operation not targeted. It also interprets missing-observation statistics and adds explicit material modeling as future work.

D1.justification: Appendices D–H disclose full VLM prompts, the Qwen checkpoint and decoding settings, 8-FPS reconstruction, confidence filtering, missing-observation handling, model dimensions, optimizer scheduling, EMA, H100 allocations, runtime measurements, and detailed user-study instructions. These substantially improve reproducibility without demonstrating changes to the existing implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including StereoFoley, FoleySpace, additional audiovisual-alignment and VLM work, and sources supporting the supplementary benchmarks. The central positioning against appearance-driven generation and narrowly physics-conditioned approaches remains intact; the additions do not redefine the claimed contribution.

P1.justification: v2 adds a structured A–J supplement with extensive explanations of existing modules, conditioning, prompts, metric computation, training, and study procedures. This substantially expands the exposition. Main-text edits are smaller, including compressed related work, wording corrections, and a new acknowledgments section.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures S1–S6 and Tables S1–S8, including estimator and robustness plots, a detailed transformer diagram, additional spectrogram panels, and configuration, runtime, result, and prompt tables. Figures 1–3 and the main table structures are retained with local layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v1 asserts estimator reliability and refers to supporting supplementary details absent from the supplied PDF. v2 provides estimator benchmarks, APCC validation, missing/noisy-cue tests, and extensive reproduction instructions, while documenting computational and visibility limitations and enlarging the user study. These resolve substantial evidential and reproducibility gaps. Proxy velocity validation and absent repeated-run uncertainty remain limitations, but do not outweigh the gains.
